top_story.headline: Federal prison in Mississippi plans to hire FlixBus, the intercity bus company, without competition
top_story.dek: The Bureau of Prisons says FlixBus North America is the only provider that can run scheduled bus service for its Yazoo City complex.
paragraphs: The Federal Bureau of Prisons, through the Federal Correctional Complex Yazoo City in Mississippi, posted a notice of intent on November 3 to award a firm-fixed-price sole-source contract for fiscal year 2027 "commercial long-distance bus transportation services" to FlixBus North America. The notice describes scheduled passenger bus routing to and from the prison complex for "critical operational transportation needs, official passenger movement, and regional transport connectivity." No dollar value is given. It was posted as a Special Notice rather than as a Justification.

The stated basis is that only one responsible source can meet the need. According to the notice, FlixBus is "the sole provider capable of meeting the government's specific requirement due to its proprietary intercity network and established commercial routes passing directly through the immediate geographic footprint of Yazoo City." It adds that any other vendor would require "a custom, non-commercial route approach." USAspending has no federal contract on record under the name FlixBus North America since fiscal year 2008, which makes a consumer bus brand an unusual sole-source vendor for a federal prison.

The notice invites other firms to submit capability statements by November 18, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. (the document gives both Eastern and Central time), and says the government alone decides whether to compete the work.

paragraphs: One item is tied to the Executive Office of the President today: a sources-sought request for information from its Office of Administration. The only attached file has not been read yet, so the notice text is all there is to go on.

blocks.title: Executive Office of the President's Office of Administration asks industry about a workflow and ticket management system
meta: Executive Office of the President, Office of Administration
blocks.text: The Executive Office of the President's Office of Administration posted a Request for Information titled "Workflow/Ticket Management System" (solicitation 11316027N0001EOP). The notice text says only that it is a request for information and points readers to an attached RFI for instructions. That attachment is queued to be read in a later edition, so what the system would track, how large it would be and whether a contract is planned are not yet known.

sections.headline: Navy plans to book the Kellogg Conference Hotel at Gallaudet University on Capitol Hill without competition
paragraphs: Four items remain tagged to Washington, D.C.: one solicitation, two presolicitations and one sources-sought notice. Three others were moved out: an Export-Import Bank justification for work in Mexico (Washington is only its headquarters) is in Sole-Source Justifications, and a National Institutes of Health notice that merely mentions the metro area is in Sources Sought. One notice already listed in an earlier edition was left out.

blocks.title: Navy says only the Kellogg Conference Hotel on Capitol Hill can host a defense conference near the Pentagon
meta: Naval Supply Systems Command Fleet Logistics Center Norfolk
blocks.text: The Naval Supply Systems Command Fleet Logistics Center Norfolk posted a sole-source notice (N0018927QD007, titled "IFLEX") saying The Kellogg Conference Hotel at Gallaudet University on Capitol Hill "is the only source able to satisfy the agencies requirements." The notice cites closeness to the Pentagon, guest lodging, group dining, indoor and outdoor fitness facilities, meeting spaces, adequate security and staff trained on defibrillators. It also says most conference speakers come from the Pentagon or the District, so holding the event near the National Capital Region "keeps transportation costs to near zero," and that the hotel sits on a closed campus. The one attachment is still queued for reading.
Also worth a look

sections.headline: Army would pay Georgia's national disease control center to supply utilities to its Tbilisi research lab without competition
paragraphs: There are 53 new sole-source justifications, 29 of them posted under other notice types such as Special Notice and Award Notice, and 35 repeats from earlier editions were left out. The FlixBus bus contract is today's Top Story and six continuing-contract items are in Extensions. Nothing here is a protest or a public-interest waiver, but several involve unusual vendors, wartime urgency and a $498 million ceiling increase.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Army research institute plans to pay Georgia's national disease control center for utilities at a shared Tbilisi laboratory, no competition
meta: National Center of Disease Control and Public Health
only one company can do it
blocks.text: The Defense Health Agency's contracting activity, buying for the Walter Reed Army Institute of Research, intends to negotiate on a sole-source basis with the National Center of Disease Control and Public Health, a Georgian government health body at 16 Kakheti Highway in Tbilisi. The Army institute's Europe-Middle East office shares the Richard M. Lugar Center for Public Health Research with that agency, which is responsible for paying the utility provider for natural gas, electricity, water and waste management. The notice says the service will keep the center running to "international bio-safety standards." If no one else responds by 2:00 p.m. Eastern on November 17, 2026, the contract goes to the center. USAspending shows an earlier federal contract under this name (first on record in 2003), so it is not a first-time vendor.

blocks.title: Air Force sole-sources an urgent power upgrade at a Shaw Air Force Base command facility, citing Operation Epic Fury
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: The 20th Contracting Squadron at Shaw Air Force Base in South Carolina is awarding Stanley Drake Construction the repair and upgrade of electrical power in Building 1921, which the justification describes as a facility for secure operations, intelligence processing and command and control. The work covers generators, transformers, switchgear, backup power and transfer switches. The justification says the need is "magnified by the current conflict in the Middle East, which has already resulted in significant American casualties," and ties the work to Operation EPIC FURY in the U.S. Central Command area. It is dated March 19, 2026 and was posted today as a Special Notice.

blocks.title: Army Corps adds $498 million to a construction contract pool for Missile Defense Agency power enclosures, open only to its 21 holders
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The U.S. Army Engineering and Support Center, Huntsville wants to raise the shared capacity of its Facilities Repair and Renewal VI multiple-award contract from $450 million to $948 million, according to the justification, "to execute critical emergent requirements in support of" the Missile Defense Agency's Modular Power Enclosures Program. The center says it received the requirement around June 17, 2026, that all task orders must be awarded before the end of March 2027 with work finished by February 2028, and that only the existing 21 holders can start immediately. Guidance cited came from the Office of the Secretary of War on July 9, 2026. No time is added to the contract.

blocks.title: Air Force picks the Catholic Diocese of Wichita, with no competition, to supply a priest for McConnell Air Force Base
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The 22nd Contracting Squadron at McConnell Air Force Base made a single-source determination for Roman Catholic priest services for the base chapel: scheduled masses, reconciliation, pastoral support, funerals and other chapel support. It says the Catholic Diocese of Wichita is the only known source that can supply a priest in good ecclesiastical standing, authorized to minister in the diocese, with continuity of service if he becomes unavailable. Market research ran from June 10 to October 22, 2026, and "other sources were identified" but did not meet the complete requirement. The $280,000 value is under the simplified acquisition threshold.

blocks.title: NASA gives Draper Laboratory a five-year, $95 million follow-on for spacecraft guidance work with no competition
meta: The Charles Stark Draper Laboratory, Inc.

blocks.text: The NASA Johnson Space Center will issue The Charles Stark Draper Laboratory a single-award indefinite-delivery contract for guidance, navigation and control work on Orion, Gateway and the Artemis campaign. The justification gives a five-year ordering period from June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2031, and says its predecessor contracts were also sole-source awards. It says Draper's Apollo heritage and embedded staff mean a transition would take "at least 2 or more years." A separate $18 million ceiling increase on the current Draper contract is listed below.

sections.headline: General Services Administration extends a military family outreach contract without competition after a protest froze its replacement
paragraphs: Six new justifications keep an incumbent running: three bridges or extensions after a protest, a funding gap or an exhausted option, and three smaller ones.

blocks.title: General Services Administration bridges Miracle Systems' military family outreach contract after a Government Accountability Office protest
meta: skipped the competition among existing contract holders
blocks.text: The justification adds option periods 3 through 6 to the bridge task order for Military Community and Family Policy outreach and digital services, which sits on the OASIS Unrestricted Pool 1 contract. It says "on September 2, 2026, a post-award protest for this solicitation was filed with the U.S. Government Accountability Office," triggering an automatic stay on the competitive successor contract and leaving no time to compete the bridge.

blocks.title: Health Resources and Services Administration buys six more months for its practitioner data bank help desk from Sparksoft, no competition
blocks.text: The agency has used up the extension allowed under FAR 52.217-8 and the current order ends November 30, 2026. The new order has a three-month base and one three-month option, for up to six months and $937,948 including the General Services Administration access fee, under the Polaris contract. It supports the National Practitioner Data Bank while a competitive follow-on is completed.

blocks.title: Marine Corps keeps leased copiers running through Cartridge Technologies after the shutdown cut funding
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: Marine Corps Installations East and II Marine Expeditionary Force are bridging multi-function device leasing and support. The determination says that after "the extended Government shutdown at the beginning of fiscal year 2026," many activities could not fund devices supplied through the Defense Logistics Agency, and a policy exception let other contracting offices keep the regional provider.

sections.headline: General Services Administration seeks a contractor to seismically retrofit the San Juan federal courthouse while it stays open

sections.headline: NASA adds $91 million for Boeing's Space Launch System stages contract
paragraphs: From this morning's edition: USAspending.gov is pulled once a day.

There were no new awards of $2 million or more (none from the Defense backlog), one large modification and one cut. The cut, a $14.0 million deduction on an Electric Boat contract signed July 21, and the other routine action are listed in "USAspending: Every Other New Award" at the end of the edition.

blocks.text: The Boeing Company received a $91,000,000 modification (P00179) from the National Aeronautics and Space Administration on October 28.
